caption: 01 · IDENTIFY — Which name is this?. Separate the person's legal name, professional name, signature, portrait, label name, house name, monogram, product line, domain, and social handle. Similar public presentation does not make these one legal object.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping which name is this? within Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · LOCATE — Where is control recorded?. For a U.S. federal mark, inspect the registration and any recorded assignments; for the company, inspect governing records; for domains and accounts, inspect registrant and administrator access; for licenses and approvals, inspect executed agreements. Never substitute the label display for the record.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping where is control recorded? within Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · DISTINGUISH — What power does each record confer?. Registration, ownership, licensed use, consent, approval, corporate voting, employment authority, account administration, and archive access answer different questions. A founder can possess some and not others.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what power does each record confer? within Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · ESCALATE — What cannot this audit decide?. Common-law rights, state publicity law, foreign law, contractual interpretation, beneficial ownership, validity, priority, and disputed facts require jurisdiction-specific investigation and qualified counsel. The map prepares that review; it does not replace it.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what cannot this audit decide? within Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It?.

caption: Separating the name into assets can make identity look purely transactional. A personal name also carries dignity, biography, community meaning, and reputational stakes that a registry cannot fully describe. Conversely, emotional identification with a label cannot resolve an ownership dispute. The exhibition keeps both truths visible without converting either into a legal conclusion.
